speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: asked the Minister for Health in each of the last five years including year-to-date, what is the number of (i) nursing homes (ii) nursing home beds and (iii) available beds and average occupancy rate, broken down by the public, not-for-profit and private sectors respectively.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Annual statistics on nursing homes are published by the Ministry of Health (MOH) on its website.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The number of available beds differs based on operational considerations.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, perhaps, if there are special circumstances and situations that he might want to highlight, he can actually send the information to us, we can take a look.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: It would be quite unusual for someone to have to wait years just to get into a nursing home.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: That is not my experience working in the hospitals as well, so I think that is quite unusual.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But what we want to do is to make sure that we do not entrench our elderly in institutions as they age.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: It is more important to make sure that they age in place and also, have good health to be able to carry on a meaningful life in their golden years.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, it is important to make sure that the intervention is about keeping them healthy, making sure that if they do have care needs, try and localise them within the community, so that they do have a social support network around them to promote emotional, physical well-being as well, such as keeping active and having engagements, rather than think about institutionalising them in nursing homes.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: That, in my mind, as a doctor, should be the very last resort for our elderly to be in.
